channel.description: This is a randomly ordered feed of the most recent entries from summarizedStoriesMainNLscienceAndDiscovery, skipping any feeds with errors.

item.title: Stress hormone may aid brain repair
item.description: A stress-related signal could help the brain heal after injury, as myelin-producing cells respond rapidly to this cue.

item.title: Immune cells invade aging brain, Stanford finds
item.description: Stanford researchers discovered that the aging brain is not as isolated from the body as previously thought, with immune cells flooding in.

item.title: Scientists detect a nuclear reactor's ghostly afterglow for the first time
item.description: Even after shutdown, nuclear fuel emits a faint antineutrino glow. Researchers have now detected this residual radiation for the first time.

item.title: Women taking estrogen had fewer signs of Alzheimer's in their brains
item.description: Women who used estrogen-only hormone therapy later in life showed reduced dementia risk and fewer Alzheimer's brain markers.
